blocks.content: A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed from his office by an order of the President.

rows: Speaker may admit or refuse the motion
Chairman may admit or refuse the motion

items: Grounds for removal are strictly limited to 'proved misbehaviour' or 'incapacity'—the term 'impeachment' is implicitly used in common parlance but explicitly specified in the Constitution only for the President.
The Speaker or Chairman has full discretion to either admit or refuse to admit the removal motion.
No judge of the Supreme Court of India has been successfully impeached to date.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A judge of the Supreme Court or High Court can be removed only on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
The procedure for removal is regulated by the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.
The removal motion must be signed by at least 100 members in the Lok Sabha or 50 members in the Rajya Sabha.
A three-member committee consisting of a Supreme Court judge, a High Court Chief Justice, and a distinguished jurist investigates the charges.
The removal address must be passed by each House of Parliament by a special majority and presented to the President in the same session.
